minutes.headline: Planning Board endorsed an ANR at 1387 Mass Ave, added a master plan member, and decided to prioritize water and battery storage bylaws.
minutes.summary: The board endorsed an ANR plan combining two parcels, appointed Kim Duffy to the master plan steering committee, and continued the homeman certificates of completion to Feb 26 pending an engineer's letter. Most of the meeting was discussion of the spring town meeting workload: the board agreed to pursue the water supply protection district rewrite and a battery energy storage bylaw, with solar overall only if feasible, and scenic roads deferred. A public hearing was tentatively planned for March 25.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board voted 4-0 to endorse an approval-not-required plan combining two parcels at 1387 Massachusetts Avenue into one lot.
The board reached consensus to pursue a water supply protection district bylaw and a battery energy storage bylaw for spring town meeting, solar only if feasible, scenic roads deferred.
The board voted 4-0 to continue the certificates of completion and performance guarantee release for 147 and 159 Homan to February 26, awaiting the engineer's written confirmation.
The board voted 4-0 to appoint Kim Duffy to the master plan steering committee.
A tentative schedule was set: notice by March 11 and a public hearing on March 25, with continuations April 8 or April 22.

why_it_matters: The bylaws the board chose to bring forward are the ones residents may be asked to vote on at spring town meeting, and the ones set aside, scenic roads and most solar, will not be on that warrant.
The Homan bond release is held until an engineer confirms the work, which keeps the performance guarantee in place until then.
watch_next: February 26: the board returns to the Homan certificates of completion and guarantee release.
March 25: tentative public hearing on the spring town meeting bylaws, with notice due by March 11.
